description: Design visibility and layout overhaul — remove section-level scroll-gating, refactor hero to two-column layout, apply alternating section backgrounds, fix mobile contact form ordering, and make services page fully static.

userStories.title: Remove section-level AnimatedSection wrappers from homepage sections
userStories.description: As a site visitor, I want all homepage section content to be visible on load so that I can read the page without scrolling or waiting for JavaScript-triggered animations.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove all AnimatedSection wrappers that enclose entire section content blocks (heading + grid/list together) from: DashboardSection, ServicesSection, HowItWorksSection, WhyUsSection, FAQSection, CTABand
Each section's content renders fully visible on load — no opacity:0 or transform applied to section-level wrappers
AnimatedSection is NOT removed from HeroSection's LocalPackCard — that is handled in US-039
CustomerJourneySection motion.divs (SVG animated lines and funnel elements) are left untouched — they animate individual decorative elements, not content blocks
All section content remains structurally correct and styled correctly after wrapper removal
curl http://localhost:3000 | grep 'opacity: 0' returns 0 matches
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: scroll homepage and confirm all sections are visible without scrolling to trigger them
userStories.notes: AnimatedSection is NOT deleted — it stays in the codebase for future individual-element use. Only its usage as a section-level content gate is removed. The useMounted + useReducedMotion guards in AnimatedSection.tsx stay intact.

userStories.title: Remove AnimatedSection from services page
userStories.description: As a site visitor on the services page, I want each service section's content to be visible immediately when I scroll to it, so that I don't see blank space before content appears.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove the AnimatedSection wrapper from inside the ServiceSection render component in app/services/page.tsx
Each service section's content (heading, description, feature list) renders fully visible as soon as the section enters the viewport — no opacity:0 gating
The StickyServiceNav component and its IntersectionObserver scroll-tracking logic remain completely intact and functional
The sticky nav correctly highlights the active service section as the user scrolls
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: navigate to /services and confirm all service section content is visible on scroll without animation delay
userStories.notes: The services page is scroll-based with a sticky nav — not a tab system. The IntersectionObserver that drives the sticky nav must not be touched. Only the AnimatedSection wrapper inside the ServiceSection render component is removed.

userStories.title: Fix mobile contact form order and remove AnimatedSection from contact page
userStories.description: As a mobile user navigating to /contact to book a call, I want the form to be the first thing I see, so that I can start filling it out immediately without scrolling past trust content.
acceptanceCriteria: On mobile (< md breakpoint), the booking form column appears above the trust signals column
On desktop (>= md breakpoint), trust signals remain on the left and the form remains on the right — no change to desktop layout
Implement using CSS order utilities: add order-first md:order-last to the form column div, add order-last md:order-first to the trust signals column div
Remove all AnimatedSection wrappers from app/contact/page.tsx (both the hero section and the two-column section)
The contact form fields, service toggle pills, and submit button all render visible on mobile without scrolling
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: resize browser to 375px, navigate to /contact, confirm form is visible above the fold without scrolling
userStories.notes: The two-column grid (grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2) stays as-is. Only the column order changes on mobile. The ContactForm component itself does not need to change.

userStories.title: Refactor hero section to two-column layout
userStories.description: As a site visitor, I want to see the Google local pack widget alongside the hero headline without scrolling, so that I immediately understand the value Foundational AI Systems delivers.
acceptanceCriteria: HeroSection refactored from a single centered column to a two-column layout at the md breakpoint
Left column contains: headline (h1), subtext paragraph, CTA buttons, TrustBar
Right column contains: LocalPackCard, visible on load with no AnimatedSection wrapper
On mobile (< md): single column, text first, LocalPackCard below — both fully visible
On desktop (>= md): left column is text/CTAs, right column is the LocalPackCard — both visible immediately on load
The AnimatedSection wrapper around LocalPackCard in HeroSection is removed
LocalPackCard is still visible and correctly styled in both breakpoints
TrustBar remains visible below the CTAs in the left column
The existing grid background (gold grid lines) remains intact
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: at 1280px confirm LocalPackCard is visible alongside the headline without scrolling; at 375px confirm text is above LocalPackCard and both are visible
userStories.notes: The min-h-[90vh] constraint on the hero section should be re-evaluated — the two-column layout is shorter vertically and may not need it. Adjust or remove if the layout looks cramped. The LocalPackCard SVG SMIL animations (gold pin pulse rings) continue to work as they are pure SVG with no JS dependency.

userStories.title: Apply alternating section backgrounds across homepage
userStories.description: As a site visitor, I want visually distinct section backgrounds as I scroll down the homepage, so that I can orient myself and feel clear progress through the page.
acceptanceCriteria: Homepage sections alternate between #021524 and #0e2131 backgrounds in this order: HeroSection (#021524), CustomerJourneySection (#0e2131), ServicesSection (#021524), HowItWorksSection (#0e2131), WhyUsSection (#021524), FAQSection (#0e2131), CTABand (#021524)
Background color is applied to the <section> element's className in each component file — not injected from page.tsx
The CTABand retains its existing gold glow/accent styling on top of the #021524 background
No section has a visible seam or gap between it and the adjacent section
The visual distinction between #021524 and #0e2131 is visible but subtle — no jarring contrast
All other section styles (padding, text colors, card backgrounds) remain unchanged
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: scroll the full homepage and confirm alternating backgrounds create clear visual section breaks
userStories.notes: Both colors already exist in the design token set and are used throughout the site (cards, pills, form backgrounds use #0e2131). This change only touches the section-level background. No new colors are introduced.
